strings.name: Brian Moynihan
strings.role: Chair and CEO of Bank of America
strings.summary: Brian Moynihan is an American lawyer and banking executive who became Bank of America's CEO in 2010 and chair in 2014. He progressed from legal and financial-business management roles to group leadership and has served as chancellor, leading Brown University's governing body, since 2024.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026, using the October quarterly results and November 6 university renewal announcement. His presidency of the bank ended in 2025. Brown's chancellor is distinct from its president, who leads daily administration; the renewed term beginning in 2027 has not started.
strings.influence.rationale: Has long led Bank of America, advancing risk management and changes to retail banking after the financial crisis.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: He earned a BA in history from Brown University in 1981 and a JD from the University of Notre Dame Law School in 1984.
strings.facts.f2.label: University governance responsibilities
strings.facts.f2.value: As Brown's chancellor, he leads its governing body, working on policy and long-term planning. The president handles daily administration.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Management across banking businesses
strings.highlights.h1.text: He led wealth management, corporate and investment banking, and consumer operations before leading the group. Business results reflect the work of management teams and employees.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Long-term governance and succession
strings.highlights.h2.text: The bank appointed two co-presidents in 2025. At Brown, he co-chairs the presidential selection committee with Pamela Ress Reeves.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Renewal as Brown chancellor announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: His second three-year term will start on July 1, 2027 and run through June 2030. It had not begun when announced.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Comments on quarterly operations
strings.timeline.t2.text: The results release includes his views on client business and AI use. Reported quarterly net income was $6.9 billion, including a $1.2 billion regulatory settlement charge, distinct from adjusted profit.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Announces co-president appointments
strings.timeline.t3.text: Dean Athanasia and Jim DeMare are appointed co-presidents. Moynihan remains chair and CEO; no departure as CEO that day is announced.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes Brown chancellor
strings.timeline.t4.text: He succeeds Samuel Mencoff as head of the university's governing body. The appointment to this volunteer role was announced in February.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Adds Bank of America chairmanship
strings.timeline.t5.text: He succeeds Charles Holliday with immediate effect. The board also introduces a lead independent director arrangement.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Bank of America president and CEO
strings.timeline.t6.text: He succeeds Kenneth Lewis and joins the board. The appointment was announced on December 16, 2009; his chairmanship has not yet begun.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Leads Global Wealth and Investment Management
strings.timeline.t7.text: Following the Fleet–Bank of America merger, he serves as president of this business until October 2007.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins Fleet predecessor institution
strings.timeline.t8.text: He moves from a law firm to Fleet Financial, initially as deputy general counsel, before moving into strategy and business management.
